short_description: A lightweight LED headlamp that gives you bright, hands-free light on pre-dawn climbs, summit nights and evenings at camp. The adjustable band fits comfortably over a beanie or cap, and the beam follows wherever you look, so you can hike, cook and set up camp safely after dark in Kenya.
description:
The best hikes in Kenya often start in the dark. A sunrise climb up Mt Longonot, the 3 a.m. push to Point Lenana or a late walk back to camp at Hell's Gate all leave you on the trail without daylight. Holding a phone torch in one hand while you scramble over rocks is awkward and unsafe. An LED headlamp puts a bright beam exactly where you're looking and leaves both hands free for trekking poles, ropes or your morning cup of tea.

This LED headlamp sits on an adjustable elastic band that fits comfortably over your head, a beanie or a cap. The light points wherever you turn your head, so you can see the path in front of your feet, read a map or find gear in your tent. LED bulbs give a strong, clear light while using little power, which is why they've replaced old filament torches for almost every outdoor use.

Why Choose This LED Headlamp?

Hands-free light changes how you move at night. With an LED headlamp, you can hike, cook, pitch a tent or change a tyre without juggling a torch. It's also one of the most important safety items on any early-morning or overnight hike, because tripping on loose stones or roots is far more likely when you can't see clearly. Runners use it for early training before work, and campers rely on it from dusk until they fall asleep.

If you want a light that charges by cable and handles heavier rain, compare it with our Waterproof Rechargeable Headlamp. For camp cooking after dark, pair your LED headlamp with a Cadac 500g Gas Cartridge for a reliable flame.

Key Features

  • Bright LED light for clear vision in the dark
  • Hands-free design that follows where you look
  • Adjustable elastic headband for a secure fit
  • Comfortable to wear over a beanie or cap
  • Lightweight and compact for any pack or pocket
  • Suitable for hiking, running, camping and home use

Benefits

Here's what an LED headlamp adds to your outdoor kit:

  • Both hands free: Use trekking poles, cook or set up camp without holding a torch.
  • Safer night hiking: See roots, rocks and loose ground before you step on them.
  • Light where you look: The beam turns with your head, so you never point it the wrong way.
  • Efficient LED power: Bright light with less drain than old-style bulbs.
  • Useful at home too: Handy during power cuts, car repairs and DIY jobs.

Perfect For

  • Sunrise and pre-dawn hikes
  • Summit nights on high mountains
  • Camping and moving around the campsite
  • Early-morning and evening running
  • Fishing, caving and night walks
  • Power outages and roadside repairs

Where to Use an LED Headlamp in Kenya

An LED headlamp is essential on Mt Kenya, where the summit push to Point Lenana usually starts around 2 or 3 a.m. so you reach the top for sunrise. The same goes for Mt Kilimanjaro's summit night. Closer to Nairobi, many groups start Mt Longonot, Ngong Hills and Elephant Hill in the dark to catch the sunrise and avoid the midday heat.

On camping trips at Hell's Gate, Lake Naivasha, Amboseli or the Aberdares, you'll use it every evening for cooking, finding gear and walking to the washrooms. Runners on the Karura Forest trails and early commuters on unlit roads also benefit from being seen and seeing clearly.

LEDs are now the standard light source for headlamps because they're efficient, durable and long-lasting. You can read more about how they work in this overview of light-emitting diodes. For anyone who hikes before dawn or camps overnight, an LED headlamp is a small, light item you'll use on every trip.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need an LED headlamp for hiking in Kenya?

For any hike that starts before sunrise or finishes after dark, yes. It's also on the required kit list for Mt Kenya and Kilimanjaro summit nights, and it's a smart backup on day hikes in case you're delayed.

Is a headlamp better than a torch?

For hiking and camping, yes. A headlamp keeps both hands free and points the light where you look, while a torch ties up one hand and has to be aimed separately.

Can I wear it over a hat?

Yes. The adjustable band fits over a beanie, cap or balaclava, which is useful on cold summit nights.

How do I make the battery last on a trek?

Switch the LED headlamp off whenever you don't need it, keep it warm inside your jacket on cold nights, and carry spare power for longer trips. Message us and we'll confirm the power type for this model.
